messages:
eli: Quick follow-up from the kernel/attention RFC review — we need a concrete plan for per-model rollout gating and graceful degradation. Thinking: feature flags + per-model circuit breaker + ordered fallback kernels.

priya: +1. Key questions: how do we express fallback order w/o exploding config? and how do we avoid cache/kv invalidation surprises when we switch kernels?

sasha: For fallback order we can use a ranked list per model group. Example: primary -> quant-v2, secondary -> quant-v1, tertiary -> cpu-fallback. Keep it declarative.

kai: Re KV cache: switching kernel families can invalidate KV cache if tokenizer or kv layout differs. We should attach a cache-fingerprint to the model-version+kernel combo and treat mismatch as cache-miss (not error). That means a brief latency bump but no correctness issue.

anu: Can we circuit-break earlier on errors than on latency? Ops prefers error_rate threshold first, then latency. E.g., if error_rate > 2% over 1m we switch to fallback.

priya: I like error-first. But also need a recovery policy: cool-down + canary traffic. Proposed state machine: ENABLED -> CANARY (1%) -> UNSTABLE (throttle) -> FALLBACK -> ROLLBACK or PROMOTE.

eli: Nice. How do we author these rules? My thought: a small DSL in our runtime config that maps model_selector -> rollout_policy. Minimal example: 
```
policies:
  - selector: model: "rw-*-base"
    allow: ["quant-v2","quant-v1","cpu-fallback"]
    circuit_breaker:
      error_rate: 0.02
      latency_ms: 350
    recovery:
      canary_pct: 1
      cool_down_s: 300
```
This is intentionally simple.

ben: Make sure selector supports labels/tags too (dedicated vs hosted) so enterprise customers can opt-out. Also need an override precedence: per-model > team > global.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline notice: new flag-schema.yaml will be validated by infra-lint in the next deploy window. See /alerts for schema issues.

jordan: What monitoring do we tie the rollouts to? We need token-level cost delta, p50/p99 latency, error types (OOM vs runtime exception), and quality regression signals (evaluations).

priya: Agreed. Instruments: kernel_switch_event with tags {model, old_kernel, new_kernel, reason}; circuit_breaker_trigger; fallback_count. Hook these to the rollout dashboard and to pager thresholds.

kai: One gotcha: when fallback moves from GPU quant to CPU, throughput drops a lot. We should have a degrade-policy that reduces request concurrency and rejects or queues long requests when throughput can't match SLA. Otherwise you'll trigger cascading failures.

anu: Also add a per-customer rate cap so a fallback doesn't starve other tenants. We have that primitive already in routing. Just wire it to the rollout engine.

eli: Two operational asks: (1) an on-call playbook snippet for fallback events; (2) an automated canary promotion step if no errors in X minutes. I'll draft both.

priya: I'll own the DSL implementation and validation. Kai and Sasha can handle cache fingerprinting and kv behavior. Anu will wire SRE alarms. Ben will add config precedence logic. Eli will draft playbook. Ops-bot will run validation on PRs.

ben: Question: do we allow manual per-model force-enable for experimental kernels? If yes, require explicit opt-in flag and audit log.

eli: Yes — manual opt-ins allowed but must be explicit and require manager approval for dedicated accounts. We'll add audit entries to the console.

priya: Implementation concerns: we should keep the runtime decision path cheap (one hash lookup + small policy eval). No heavy rule engine.

kai: For kernel chooser v2, we can precompute compiled policy tables periodically and ship to runtime nodes. That keeps runtime O(1) per request.

eli: Action items recap: 
1) Priya: PR for policy schema + validator (ETA 2d)
2) Kai/Sasha: cache-fingerprint design doc (ETA 3d)
3) Anu: alert thresholds and playbook stub (ETA 2d)
4) Ben: precedence/override rules + console audit hooks (ETA 4d)
5) Eli: playbook + rollout runbook (ETA 1d)

priya: I'll open tracking tickets and a small RFC to record the DSL and state machine.

eli: Thanks all. If no objections, we'll target a small canary next week behind feature flags. :thumbsup:
